verdicts.reason: A: the logo is shrunk to a tiny mark wedged beside the legal block. The price is set nearly as big as the headline, so the two compete. The tagline leaves an orphaned "m." on its own line, the watch is jammed against the left edge, and the headline, price and copy are stacked with no breathing room. B: the headline breaks into four one-word lines and runs right to the bottom edge, and the watch strap gets cut off. The right column is cramped from top to bottom: copy touching the top edge, the price wrapping, an oversized CTA and dense legal text. Still, the logo survives intact and the three columns read in a clear order (brand/product, then message, then action), so B is less broken.
